why: Abandonment as a legal separation ground needs MORE THAN ONE YEAR. The three-month period is the Art. 101 presumption for judicial separation of property.

original: (10) Abandonment of petitioner by respondent without justifiable cause for more than one year.
altered: (10) Abandonment of petitioner by respondent for more than one year.
why: Abandonment must be WITHOUT JUSTIFIABLE CAUSE.

original: (4) Where both parties have given ground for legal separation;
altered: (4) Where either party has given ground for legal separation;
why: Mutual guilt (recrimination) bars the action only if BOTH parties have given ground.

original: An action for legal separation shall be filed within five years from the time of the occurrence of the cause.
altered: An action for legal separation shall be filed within ten years from the time of the occurrence of the cause.
why: The prescriptive period is FIVE years. Prescription is a ground for denial under Art. 56(6).

original: An action for legal separation shall be filed within five years from the time of the occurrence of the cause.
altered: An action for legal separation shall be filed within five years from the time of the discovery of the cause.
why: The five years run from the OCCURRENCE of the cause, not its discovery (contrast Art. 47(3), fraud).

original: An action for legal separation shall in no case be tried before six months shall have elapsed since the filing of the petition.
altered: An action for legal separation shall in no case be tried before three months shall have elapsed since the filing of the petition.
why: The cooling-off period is SIX months from filing. It does not apply where VAWC violence is alleged (RA 9262, Sec. 19).

original: No decree of legal separation shall be based upon a stipulation of facts or a confession of judgment.
altered: A decree of legal separation shall be based upon a stipulation of facts or a confession of judgment.
why: NO decree may be based on a stipulation of facts or a confession of judgment. The prosecutor guards against collusion.

original: After the filing of the petition for legal separation, the spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other.
altered: After the filing of the petition for legal separation, the spouses shall not be entitled to live separately from each other.
why: The spouses may live separately right after the PETITION is FILED. They need not wait for the decree.

original: (1) The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other, but the marriage bonds shall not be severed;
altered: (1) The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other, but the marriage bonds shall be severed;
why: Legal separation does NOT sever the marriage bond, so neither spouse may remarry.

original: (4) The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate succession. Moreover, provisions in favor of the offending spouse made in the will of the innocent spouse shall be revoked by operation of law.
altered: (4) The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by testate and intestate succession. Moreover, provisions in favor of the offending spouse made in the will of the innocent spouse shall be revoked by operation of law.
why: Under Art. 63(4), the disqualification is from INTESTATE succession only, while provisions in the will are revoked by law. Contrast Art. 43(5), which bars both testate and intestate succession.

original: After the finality of the decree of legal separation, the innocent spouse may revoke the donations made by him or by her in favor of the offending spouse, as well as the designation of the latter as beneficiary in any insurance policy, even if such designation be stipulated as irrevocable.
altered: After the finality of the decree of legal separation, the innocent spouse may revoke the donations made by him or by her in favor of the offending spouse, as well as the designation of the latter as beneficiary in any insurance policy, unless such designation be stipulated as irrevocable.
why: Revocation is allowed EVEN IF the designation is stipulated as irrevocable. Revocation is optional ('may'), unlike the revocation by operation of law in Art. 43(3).

original: The action to revoke the donation under this Article must be brought within five (5) years from the time the decree of legal separation has become final.
altered: The action to revoke the donation under this Article must be brought within one (1) year from the time the decree of legal separation has become final.
why: The action to revoke donations must be brought within FIVE years from the FINALITY of the decree.

original: If the spouses should reconcile, a corresponding joint manifestation under oath duly signed by them shall be filed with the court in the same proceeding for legal separation.
altered: If the spouses should reconcile, a corresponding joint manifestation under oath duly signed by them shall be filed with the court in a separate proceeding for legal separation.
why: The joint sworn manifestation of reconciliation is filed IN THE SAME proceeding.

original: (2) The final decree of legal separation shall be set aside, but the separation of property and any forfeiture of the share of the guilty spouse already effected shall subsist, unless the spouses agree to revive their former property regime.
altered: (2) The final decree of legal separation shall be set aside, but the separation of property and any forfeiture of the share of the guilty spouse already effected shall be restored, unless the spouses agree to revive their former property regime.
why: After reconciliation, the separation of property and forfeiture SUBSIST unless the spouses agree to revive their regime under oath (Art. 67).

original: The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the court shall decide.
altered: The husband shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the court shall decide.
why: BOTH spouses fix the family domicile. The rule under the repealed NCC Art. 110 that the husband fixes the residence no longer applies.

original: The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the court shall decide.
altered: The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the husband shall decide.
why: In case of disagreement, the COURT decides. Neither spouse has the final say.

original: The court may exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter should live abroad or there are other valid and compelling reasons for the exemption. However, such exemption shall not apply if the same is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.
altered: The court may exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter should live abroad or there are other valid and compelling reasons for the exemption. However, such exemption shall apply if the same is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.
why: The exemption does NOT apply if it is incompatible with the solidarity of the family.

original: The spouses are jointly responsible for the support of the family.
altered: The husband is primarily responsible for the support of the family.
why: BOTH spouses are jointly responsible. The order is: community property first, then the income or fruits of separate property, then the separate property itself.

original: The management of the household shall be the right and the duty of both spouses.
altered: The management of the household shall be the right and the duty of the wife.
why: Household management is the right and duty of BOTH spouses.

original: When one of the spouses neglects his or her duties to the conjugal union or commits acts which tend to bring danger, dishonor or injury to the other or to the family, the aggrieved party may apply to the court for relief.
altered: When one of the spouses neglects his or her duties to the conjugal union or commits acts which tend to bring danger, dishonor or injury to the other or to the family, the aggrieved party may apply to the court for legal separation.
why: The Art. 72 remedy is to apply to the court for RELIEF (e.g., receivership or injunction). Neglect of duties is not by itself a ground for legal separation under Art. 55.

original: Either spouse may exercise any legitimate profession, occupation, business or activity without the consent of the other. The latter may object only on valid, serious, and moral grounds.
altered: Either spouse may exercise any legitimate profession, occupation, business or activity with the consent of the other. The latter may object only on valid, serious, and moral grounds.
why: Since RA 10572 (2013), EITHER spouse may exercise a profession WITHOUT the other's consent.

original: Either spouse may exercise any legitimate profession, occupation, business or activity without the consent of the other. The latter may object only on valid, serious, and moral grounds.
altered: Either spouse may exercise any legitimate profession, occupation, business or activity without the consent of the other. The latter may not object only on valid, serious, and moral grounds.
why: The other spouse MAY object, but only on VALID, SERIOUS, AND MORAL grounds. If they disagree, the court decides.

original: If the benefit accrued prior to the objection, the resulting obligation shall be enforced against the community property. If the benefit accrued thereafter, such obligation shall be enforced against the separate property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.
altered: If the benefit accrued prior to the objection, the resulting obligation shall be enforced against the separate property. If the benefit accrued thereafter, such obligation shall be enforced against the separate property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.
why: If the benefit accrued BEFORE the objection, the obligation is enforced against the COMMUNITY property.

original: If the benefit accrued prior to the objection, the resulting obligation shall be enforced against the community property. If the benefit accrued thereafter, such obligation shall be enforced against the separate property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.
altered: If the benefit accrued prior to the objection, the resulting obligation shall be enforced against the community property. If the benefit accrued thereafter, such obligation shall be enforced against the community property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.
why: If the benefit accrued AFTER the objection, the obligation is enforced against the SEPARATE property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.

original: The foregoing provisions shall not prejudice the rights of creditors who acted in good faith.
altered: The foregoing provisions shall prejudice the rights of creditors who acted in good faith.
why: The rights of creditors in GOOD FAITH are NOT prejudiced by the spouses' disagreement.

original: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in writing, signed by the parties and executed before the celebration of the marriage.
altered: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in a public instrument, signed by the parties and executed before the celebration of the marriage.
why: Writing suffices. Asked in Quiz #3, the compilations and the Quiz 3 key.

original: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in writing, signed by the parties and executed before the celebration of the marriage.
altered: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in writing, signed by the parties and may be made before the celebration of the marriage.
why: Execution before the celebration is mandatory (CivRev 2025 Quiz 4 #5).

original: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in writing, signed by the parties and executed before the celebration of the marriage.
altered: The marriage settlements and any modification thereof shall be in writing, signed by the parties and executed during the celebration of the marriage.
why: Before, not during (Quiz #3 pair variant).

original: They shall not prejudice third persons unless they are registered in the local civil registry where the marriage contract is recorded as well as in the proper registries of properties.
altered: They shall not prejudice third persons unless they are registered in the local civil registry where the marriage contract is recorded or in the proper registries of properties.
why: Both registries are required.

original: The property relationship between husband and wife shall be governed in the following order: (1) By marriage settlements executed before the marriage; (2) By the provisions of this Code; and (3) By the local custom.
altered: The property relationship between husband and wife shall be governed in the following order: (1) By marriage settlements executed before or during the marriage; (2) By the provisions of this Code; and (3) By the local custom.
why: Only settlements executed BEFORE the marriage; changes after the wedding need the court (Arts. 76, 134).

original: A minor who according to law may contract marriage may also execute his or her marriage settlements, but they shall be valid only if the persons designated in Article 14 to give consent to the marriage are made parties to the agreement, subject to the provisions of Title IX of this Code.
altered: A minor who according to law may contract marriage may also execute his or her marriage settlements, but they shall be valid only if the persons designated in Article 15 to give consent to the marriage are made parties to the agreement, subject to the provisions of Title IX of this Code.
why: Art. 14 (consent), not Art. 15 (advice).

original: Everything stipulated in the settlements or contracts referred to in the preceding articles in consideration of a future marriage, including donations between the prospective spouses made therein, shall be rendered void if the marriage does not take place.
altered: Everything stipulated in the settlements or contracts referred to in the preceding articles in consideration of a future marriage, including donations between the prospective spouses made therein, shall be revocable if the marriage does not take place.
why: Void, not revocable (Quiz 4 #6). 'Shall be rendered void' becomes 'shall be revocable'.

original: Donations by reason of marriage are those which are made before its celebration, in consideration of the same, and in favor of one or both of the future spouses.
altered: Donations by reason of marriage are those which are made before its celebration, in consideration of the same, and made by one or both of the future spouses.
why: In favor of, not made by (Quiz 4 #9).

original: If the future spouses agree upon a regime other than the absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their present property.
altered: If the future spouses agree upon a regime of absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their present property.
why: Other than ACP (Quiz #3 pair 4).

original: If the future spouses agree upon a regime other than the absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their present property.
altered: If the future spouses agree upon a regime other than the absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their future property.
why: Present, not future (Quiz 4 #4).

original: If the future spouses agree upon a regime other than the absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their present property.
altered: If the future spouses agree upon a regime other than the absolute community of property, they cannot donate to each other in their marriage settlements more than one-fifth of their personal property.
why: Present, not personal (quiz compilation TF 5).

original: Donations of future property shall be governed by the provisions on testamentary succession and the formalities of wills.
altered: Donations of present property shall be governed by the provisions on testamentary succession and the formalities of wills.
why: Future property follows the rules on wills.

original: In case of foreclosure of the encumbrance and the property is sold for less than the total amount of the obligation secured, the donee shall not be liable for the deficiency.
altered: In case of foreclosure of the encumbrance and the property is sold for less than the total amount of the obligation secured, the donor shall not be liable for the deficiency.
why: Donee, not donor (Quiz #3 pair 3).

original: When the marriage takes place without the consent of the parents or guardian, as required by law;
altered: When the marriage takes place without the advice of the parents or guardian, as required by law;
why: Consent, not advice (Quiz 4 #16).

original: Upon legal separation, the donee being the guilty spouse;
altered: Upon legal separation, the donor being the guilty spouse;
why: Donee, not donor (Quiz 4 #16).

original: If it is with a resolutory condition and the condition is complied with;
altered: If it is with a suspensive condition and the condition is complied with;
why: Resolutory, not suspensive (Quiz 4 #16).

original: Every donation or grant of gratuitous advantage, direct or indirect, between the spouses during the marriage shall be void, except moderate gifts which the spouses may give each other on the occasion of any family rejoicing.
altered: Every donation or grant of gratuitous advantage, direct or indirect, between the spouses during the marriage shall be voidable, except moderate gifts which the spouses may give each other on the occasion of any family rejoicing.
why: Void, not voidable.

original: Any stipulation, express or implied, for the commencement of the community regime at any other time shall be void.
altered: Any stipulation, express or implied, for the commencement of the community regime at any other time shall be voidable.
why: Void.

original: No waiver of rights, shares and effects of the absolute community of property during the marriage can be made except in case of judicial separation of property.
altered: No waiver of rights, shares and effects of the absolute community of property during the marriage can be made except in case of legal separation.
why: Judicial separation of property, not legal separation.

original: The provisions on co-ownership shall apply to the absolute community of property between the spouses in all matters not provided for in this Chapter.
altered: The provisions on partnership shall apply to the absolute community of property between the spouses in all matters not provided for in this Chapter.
why: ACP: co-ownership. CPG: partnership.

original: Property for personal and exclusive use of either spouse. However, jewelry shall form part of the community property;
altered: Property for personal and exclusive use of either spouse. However, jewelry shall form part of the separate property;
why: Jewelry is community property.

original: Property acquired before the marriage by either spouse who has legitimate descendants by a former marriage, and the fruits as well as the income, if any, of such property.
altered: Property acquired before the marriage by either spouse who has descendants by a former marriage, and the fruits as well as the income, if any, of such property.
why: Legitimate descendants (deleted word: tap the word next to the gap).

original: Property acquired during the marriage is presumed to belong to the community, unless it is proved that it is one of those excluded therefrom.
altered: Property registered during the marriage is presumed to belong to the community, unless it is proved that it is one of those excluded therefrom.
why: Acquired, not registered (Quiz 4 #20).

original: All taxes and expenses for mere preservation made during marriage upon the separate property of either spouse used by the family;
altered: All taxes and expenses for mere preservation made during marriage upon the separate property of either spouse;
why: 'Used by the family' was dropped (CivRev midterms pair #3).

original: … shall be borne by the loser and shall not be charged to the community but any winnings therefrom shall form part of the community property.
altered: … shall be borne by the loser and shall be charged to the community but any winnings therefrom shall form part of the community property.
why: Losses to the loser.

original: In case of disagreement, the husband's decision shall prevail, subject to recourse to the court by the wife for proper remedy, which must be availed of within five years from the date of the contract implementing such decision.
altered: In case of disagreement, the husband's decision shall prevail, subject to recourse to the court by the wife for proper remedy, which must be availed of within one year from the date of the contract implementing such decision.
why: Five years.

original: In the absence of such authority or consent, the disposition or encumbrance shall be void.
altered: In the absence of such authority or consent, the disposition or encumbrance shall be voidable.
why: Void, but a continuing offer.

original: However, either spouse may, without the consent of the other, make moderate donations from the community property for charity or on occasions of family rejoicing or family distress.
altered: However, either spouse may, without the consent of the other, make any donations from the community property for charity or on occasions of family rejoicing or family distress.
why: Only moderate donations.

original: The spouse who has left the conjugal dwelling for a period of three months or has failed within the same period to give any information as to his or her whereabouts shall be prima facie presumed to have no intention of returning to the conjugal dwelling.
altered: The spouse who has left the conjugal dwelling for a period of three months or has failed within the same period to give any information as to his or her whereabouts shall be deemed to have no intention of returning to the conjugal dwelling.
why: Prima facie presumed, not deemed (quiz compilation TF 7).

original: If no judicial settlement proceeding is instituted, the surviving spouse shall liquidate the community property either judicially or extra-judicially within one year from the death of the deceased spouse.
altered: If no judicial settlement proceeding is instituted, the surviving spouse shall liquidate the community property either judicially or extra-judicially within six months from the death of the deceased spouse.
why: ACP: one year (CPG: six months).

original: The conjugal partnership shall be governed by the rules on the contract of partnership in all that is not in conflict with what is expressly determined in this Chapter or by the spouses in their marriage settlements.
altered: The conjugal partnership shall be governed by the rules on co-ownership in all that is not in conflict with what is expressly determined in this Chapter or by the spouses in their marriage settlements.
why: Partnership, not co-ownership (quiz compilation TF 8).

original: Either spouse may, during the marriage, transfer the administration of his or her exclusive property to the other by means of a public instrument, which shall be recorded in the registry of property of the place the property is located.
altered: Either spouse may, during the marriage, transfer the administration of his or her exclusive property to the other by means of a private instrument, which shall be recorded in the registry of property of the place the property is located.
why: Public instrument.

original: The fruits, natural, industrial, or civil, due or received during the marriage from the common property, as well as the net fruits from the exclusive property of each spouse;
altered: The fruits, natural, industrial, or civil, due or received during the marriage from the common property, but not the net fruits from the exclusive property of each spouse;
why: Net fruits of exclusive property ARE conjugal.

original: … belongs to the buyer or buyers if full ownership was vested before the marriage and to the conjugal partnership if such ownership was vested during the marriage.
altered: … belongs to the conjugal partnership if full ownership was vested before the marriage and to the conjugal partnership if such ownership was vested during the marriage.
why: Vested before the marriage → the buyer or buyers.

original: However, interests falling due during the marriage on the principal shall belong to the conjugal partnership.
altered: However, interests falling due during the marriage on the principal shall belong to the creditor-spouse.
why: Interest goes to the CPG.

original: In either case, the ownership of the entire property shall be vested upon the reimbursement, which shall be made at the time of the liquidation of the conjugal partnership.
altered: In either case, the ownership of the entire property shall be vested upon the completion of the improvement, which shall be made at the time of the liquidation of the conjugal partnership.
why: Vests upon reimbursement at liquidation.

original: The support of the spouse, their common children, and the legitimate children of either spouse; however, the support of illegitimate children shall be governed by the provisions of this Code on Support;
altered: The support of the spouse, their common children, and the children of either spouse; however, the support of illegitimate children shall be governed by the provisions of this Code on Support;
why: Legitimate children of either spouse.

original: If no judicial settlement proceeding is instituted, the surviving spouse shall liquidate the conjugal partnership property either judicially or extra-judicially within six months from the death of the deceased spouse.
altered: If no judicial settlement proceeding is instituted, the surviving spouse shall liquidate the conjugal partnership property either judicially or extra-judicially within one year from the death of the deceased spouse.
why: CPG: six months.

original: That at the time of the petition, the spouses have been separated in fact for at least one year and reconciliation is highly improbable.
altered: That at the time of the petition, the spouses have been separated in fact for at least six months and reconciliation is highly improbable.
why: One year.

original: In the latter case, the property not agreed upon as separate shall pertain to the absolute community.
altered: In the latter case, the property not agreed upon as separate shall pertain to the conjugal partnership.
why: Absolute community.

original: Both spouses shall bear the family expenses in proportion to their income, or, in case of insufficiency or default thereof, to the current market value of their separate properties.
altered: Both spouses shall bear the family expenses equally, or, in case of insufficiency or default thereof, to the current market value of their separate properties.
why: In proportion to their income.

original: The liabilities of the spouses to creditors for family expenses shall, however, be solidary.
altered: The liabilities of the spouses to creditors for family expenses shall, however, be joint.
why: Solidary.

original: … their wages and salaries shall be owned by them in equal shares and the property acquired by both of them through their work or industry shall be governed by the rules on co-ownership.
altered: … their wages and salaries shall be owned by them in proportion to their contributions and the property acquired by both of them through their work or industry shall be governed by the rules on co-ownership.
why: Equal shares.

original: When only one of the parties to a void marriage is in good faith, the share of the party in bad faith in the co-ownership shall be forfeited in favor of their common children.
altered: When only one of the parties to a void marriage is in good faith, the share of the party in bad faith in the co-ownership shall be forfeited in favor of the innocent party.
why: Common children first.

original: The foregoing rules on forfeiture shall likewise apply even if both parties are in bad faith.
altered: The foregoing rules on forfeiture shall likewise apply only if both parties are in bad faith.
why: They apply even if both are in bad faith.
